terms.comment: The sky, and the dwelling of the gods and of God. The Church often uses the plural, caelī, after the Hebrew (quī es in caelīs; Lewis & Short); the kingdom of heaven is rēgnum caelōrum. For heaven’s sake! is obsecrō (Traupman 327).
Greek παράδεισος, a park (Gell.); the garden of Eden (paradīsus voluptātis, Gen. 2.15), and the dwelling of the blessed (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Pater noster, quī es in caelīs, sānctificētur nōmen tuum.
phrases.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name.
of such is the kingdom of heaven (said over a sleeping child)
today you will be with me in paradise

sources: Lewis & Short: caelum · Lewis & Short: paradisus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 327.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. heaven.
